overrides_applied.source: Form 10-K for fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (filed 2026-02-13), consolidated statements of cash flows and MD&A Summary of Cash Flow Activity: 'Real estate development and capital improvements' $435,112 thousand in 2025 and $343,368 thousand in 2024; the 2023 figure $232,855 thousand is the same line as tagged PaymentsToDevelopRealEstateAssets in EDGAR companyfacts (10-Q YTD facts of the same tag give Q1 2025 $101,386 thousand and Q1 2026 $105,071 thousand). Regency files no PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment or any other engine candidate capex tag in any year — its capital spending is tagged PaymentsToDevelopRealEstateAssets, which the engine does not read, so the engine has no filed capex value (last_filed_value null).
overrides_applied.reason: DATA_GAP:capex — capex missing for FY2023, 2024, 2025 of the last 3 (in fact all years under engine candidate tags). The override value is the LATEST filed year's (FY2025) development-and-capital-improvements spend, because the final base is the TTM pin: ttm.py fills every capex leg with this override (no filed leg exists under its candidate tags), so the pin is only honest at the current spend level — at FY2025's $435,112 thousand the TTM pin is $2.00/share vs a true TTM of $1.98/share computed from filed 10-Q YTD development spend (FY2025 $435,112 − Q1 2025 $101,386 + Q1 2026 $105,071 = $438,797 thousand TTM spend; analysis.md), while at FY2024's $343,368 thousand the pin would read $2.50/share on a capex leg the filings contradict (spend has plateaued at the FY2025 level: Q1 2026 $105,071 thousand vs Q1 2025 $101,386 thousand). Cost of the choice, disclosed: the engine applies the one value to every gap year, so the normalized 3-yr median reads ~$1.82/share — below every filed year — an artifact; the true per-year median at each year's filed spend and filed diluted share count is $2.31/share and the true latest-FY figure is $2.05/share (analysis.md method range). Acquisitions of operating real estate ($104,153 thousand in 2025, $45,405 thousand in 2024, same statements) are excluded, consistent with the engine's convention of excluding PaymentsToAcquireBusinesses from capex for non-REIT filers.

overrides_applied.source: Form 10-K for fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (filed 2026-02-13), Note 14 Earnings per Share and Unit, 'Parent Company Earnings per Share' table (in thousands, except per share data): weighted average common shares outstanding for diluted EPS 182,234 in 2025 (183,040 in 2024; 176,371 in 2023); diluted EPS $2.82 / $2.11 / $2.04 on net income attributable to common shareholders of $513,810 / $386,738 / $359,500 thousand. EDGAR companyfacts carries no weighted-average share series for CIK 910606 after FY2020 (the filer tags share counts with dimensions the aggregated facts drop), so the engine fell back to point-in-time CommonStockSharesOutstanding counts (184,581,070 / 181,361,454 / 182,902,234).
overrides_applied.reason: DATA_GAP:shares — diluted weighted shares missing for FY2023, 2024, 2025 in companyfacts; only non-diluted outstanding counts are filed there. The filer's own FY2025 diluted weighted average count fills the gap; the engine applies this single value to every missing period (including the 2016/2021/2022 fallback history years, where it modestly understates OE/share vs the ~171M shares then outstanding — history only, not the base). The 3-yr median base is barely affected: FY2024's true diluted count (183,040,000) differs from the override by 0.4%. ttm.py uses the override unprorated as the TTM denominator — the current-period figure.

SHARES_FALLBACK: no diluted share count filed for 2016, 2021, 2022 — those history years use the basic / outstanding / dei count recorded in the shares_tag column; per-share history there is approximate
